+title: Swap the Registry in MultiTool at the turn boundary
+---
+## What
+The second half of rebuild-and-swap. eventplan.md § "Consolidation of the siblings": "Then MultiTool swaps it in atomically at the next turn boundary — the same boundary where the outbox folds in events. Nothing changes below a snippet that runs. An in-flight run keeps the registry that it started with."
+
+Router supplies the boundary through `TurnBoundaryTool.turnWillBegin()` (the Router task on this board). This task makes `MultiTool` conform and apply a staged registry there.
+
+- Modify `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/MultiTool.swift`: today `registry`, `hostFunctions`, `liveTools`, `preamble`, and `hintSearcher` are `let`s set in `init`. Group them into one `RegistryBundle` value (a new file `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/RegistryBundle.swift`) that is built from a `Registry` in one function. `MultiTool` holds the current bundle in a `Mutex` (or `OSAllocatedUnfairLock`) and reads it one time at the start of `call(arguments:)`. The run keeps that bundle to its end.
+- Add `public func stage(_ registry: Registry)`: keeps the newest staged registry, and nothing else. Add the `TurnBoundaryTool` conformance in `MultiTool+TurnBoundary.swift`: `turnWillBegin()` moves the staged registry, if any, into the current bundle. A stage with no turn between gives one swap, of the newest.
+- `SearchToolsTool` (`tools.searchTools` and the mounted `findAPIs`) reads `registry.surface.entries` for selection. Give it the same staged-and-swapped path: `Registry.makeSessionTools(...)` returns the pair, and the pair shares one holder, so the two doors swap together at the same tick.
+- `MultiTool+Forking.swift`: a fork copies the current bundle and the staged registry. Update the header comment that says the registry "never changes"; it now says the registry changes only at a turn boundary, and a run keeps the one it started with.
+- The parked runs and the mailbox are untouched: the mailbox has session scope in Router.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `stage(_:)` then `turnWillBegin()` makes the next `runCode` see the new verbs, and `help()` / `docs()` / `findAPIs` see them at the same time.
+- [ ] `stage(_:)` with no `turnWillBegin()` leaves the current surface unchanged.
+- [ ] A snippet in flight across a swap completes against the registry it started with (start a slow `ScriptedTool` call, stage, tick, and assert the run's later `tools.*` call in the same snippet resolves the old surface).
+- [ ] Two stages then one tick gives the newest registry.
+- [ ] `swift build` succeeds.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Add `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/RegistrySwapTests.swift` with the criteria above.
+- [ ] Extend `MultiToolForkingTests` (or the forking suite that exists) with a case that a fork carries the staged registry.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter RegistrySwapTests` passes.
+- [ ] Full `swift test` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the swap tests first, then implement. #eventplan #phase-4
\ No newline at end of file

+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m12ha6n47tpgm09rghpw98kh
+  text: |-
+    ### Discoveries during the implementation
+
+    - The second method is named `makeSessionToolsAndStaging(librarian:sampleGenerator:)`. An overload of `makeSessionTools` that differs in the return type alone makes the six callers ambiguous; the doc comment of the new method records this.
+    - `RegistryBundle` carries a `RegistryBundleShape` (`bindsSearchTools`, `discovery`), so `RegistryHolder.applyStaged()` builds the next bundle the same way as the first. The bundle also holds the discovery searcher of `searchTools` (`DiscoverySearch.configured(selection:)`), because `MetadataSearcher` builds its index at `init` and the selection tier is bound to the librarian. `SearchToolsTool.makeSearcher(over:selection:)`, `makeSelection(librarian:)` and `makeSample(generator:)` are the one place each of these is built; `init(registry:librarian:...)` and `makeSessionToolsAndStaging` both call them.
